options.text: The committee have reached a decision.
The committee has reached a decision.
The committee are reaching a decision.
The committee were reached a decision.

hint_ladder.title: What Kind of Word Is 'Committee'?
hint_ladder.text: Think of 'committee' as a single unit, not a bunch of individuals. It's a collective noun, like 'team' or 'family'.

hint_ladder.title: The Simple Rule for Collective Nouns
hint_ladder.text: In American English, collective nouns are treated as singular. So they pair with singular verbs like 'has', 'is', or 'reaches'.

hint_ladder.title: Spot the Singular Verb
hint_ladder.text: Look at each verb: 'have' is plural, 'has' is singular, 'are' is plural, 'were' is plural. Only one option uses a singular verb.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminate with Taglish
hint_ladder.text: Taglish tip: 'Isipin ang committee bilang isang tao. Kaya 'has' ang gamit.' Only B uses the singular 'has' correctly.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you thought of the members individually. Remember, collective nouns are singular in this exam.

B.text: Correct. 'Committee' is a singular collective noun, so it pairs perfectly with the singular verb 'has'.

C.text: You might have chosen C because 'are' sounds natural, but 'committee' as a unit requires singular verb 'has'.

D.text: You might have chosen D because of past tense, but 'were reached' is wrong verb form and plural; use 'has reached'.

next_time_rule: When you see a collective noun, treat it as singular by default. Use the 'One Unit Test': imagine the group as one person.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine your barangay’s Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) meeting. The entire committee acts as one unit, so you'd say 'The committee has reached a decision.'

In American English (the standard for this exam), collective nouns like 'committee', 'team', 'jury' are singular. They take singular verbs like 'has', not 'have', 'are', or 'were'.

Mental trick in Taglish: 'Isipin mo, ang committee ay parang iisang tao. Kaya gamitin ang ‘has,’ hindi ‘have.’' Tandaan mo: one unit = one verb.
